trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left, right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going right would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
I can't rule out up, around the edge to (1,6) or around the edge to (6,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going to number 5 would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (up from cell (6,6)) was wrong. Next I'll try around the edge to (1,6).
I can't rule out around the edge to (1,1) or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (1,1).
I can't rule out around the edge to (6,1), right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (6,1).

Contradiction! Going around the edge to (1,2) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (around the edge to (6,1) from cell (1,1)) was wrong. Next I'll try right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going around the edge to (6,2) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So my guess (right from cell (1,1)) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going around the edge to (2,6), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
The line must go up: right is number 8, which comes later; down is number 13, which comes later.
Going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2). So the line goes up.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: around the edge to (6,3) is number 12, which comes later.
Going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Cell (3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would cut off the top-right corner (4 cells). So the line goes up.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
